promptText: Which select-service hotel brands are commonly considered for new-build projects globally?

payload.rawResponseText:
“Select service” is defined somewhat differently by each hotel group—Hilton uses **focused service**, IHG uses **Essentials**, and Accor generally categorizes comparable brands as **economy or midscale**. For a global new-build feasibility study, the following brands commonly appear on the initial longlist.

## Principal global candidates

| Hotel group | Brands commonly considered | Typical positioning |
|---|---|---|
| **Marriott International** | **Courtyard**, **Fairfield by Marriott**, **Four Points by Sheraton**, **AC Hotels**, **Aloft**, **Moxy** | Upper-midscale through upscale; transient business, airport, suburban and urban-lifestyle projects |
| **Hilton** | **Hampton by Hilton**, **Hilton Garden Inn**, **Tru by Hilton** | Midscale through upscale focused service |
| **IHG Hotels & Resorts** | **Holiday Inn Express**, **avid hotels**; sometimes a streamlined **Holiday Inn** | Midscale and upper-midscale |
| **Accor** | **ibis**, **ibis Styles**, **ibis budget**, **Novotel**, **Mercure**, **TRIBE** | Economy through upper-midscale; particularly strong outside North America |
| **Hyatt** | **Hyatt Place**; sometimes **Caption by Hyatt** | Upscale select service and urban lifestyle |
| **Wyndham Hotels & Resorts** | **La Quinta**, **Wyndham Garden**, **Microtel**, **Wingate**, **AmericInn** | Economy through upper-midscale; availability varies substantially by region |
| **Radisson/Choice** | **Park Inn by Radisson**, **Country Inn & Suites**, **Prize by Radisson**, **Radisson RED**; **Comfort**, **Sleep Inn** and **Cambria** in applicable markets | Midscale through upscale lifestyle |

Marriott formally places Courtyard, Four Points, Fairfield, AC, Aloft and Moxy in its select-service portfolio. Hilton’s focused-service category comprises Hilton Garden Inn, Hampton, Tru and Spark, although Spark began primarily as a conversion proposition. IHG’s Essentials portfolio includes Holiday Inn Express, avid, Garner and Holiday Inn. ([hotel-development.marriott.com](https://www.hotel-development.marriott.com/brands/select-brands))

Accor’s principal economy and midscale development brands include the ibis family, Novotel and Mercure; these categories generated most of Accor’s 2025 openings. Hyatt identifies Hyatt Place as upscale select service, with Caption, Hyatt Select and related brands expanding its “Essentials” portfolio. ([group.accor.com](https://group.accor.com/files/2025-universal-registration-document?utm_source=openai))

Wyndham specifically markets Microtel, La Quinta, Wyndham Garden, Wingate and AmericInn as new-construction brands. Radisson’s comparable portfolio includes Park Inn, Country Inn & Suites, Prize and Radisson RED. ([development.wyndhamhotels.com](https://development.wyndhamhotels.com/build-a-new-hotel/))

## Extended-stay brands often screened alongside select service

Although technically a separate segment, these are frequently evaluated in the same feasibility exercise:

- **Marriott:** Residence Inn, Element, TownePlace Suites, SpringHill Suites  
- **Hilton:** Home2 Suites, Homewood Suites  
- **IHG:** Staybridge Suites, Candlewood Suites, Atwell Suites  
- **Hyatt:** Hyatt House, Hyatt Studios  
- **Accor:** Adagio, Novotel Living, Mercure Living  
- **Wyndham:** Hawthorn Extended Stay, ECHO Suites  
- **Choice:** Everhome Suites, WoodSpring Suites, MainStay Suites  

IHG explicitly places Staybridge, Atwell and Candlewood in its Suites portfolio, while Hilton combines Home2 and Homewood with its focused-service category organizationally. Wyndham lists ECHO and Hawthorn among its purpose-designed new-construction options. ([development.ihg.com](https://development.ihg.com/hotel-brands))

## Newer or more region-specific options

These may be relevant but are not yet as universally applicable:

- **Marriott:** City Express by Marriott, Four Points Flex, Series by Marriott, citizenM  
- **Hilton:** Spark, Motto and Tempo  
- **IHG:** Garner—generally more conversion-oriented—and avid outside its established markets  
- **Hyatt:** Hyatt Select and Hyatt Studios, currently more Americas-focused  
- **Accor:** greet and regionally deployed economy brands  
- **Choice:** Comfort, Sleep Inn, Country Inn & Suites and Cambria—strongest in North America, with selected international expansion  

Choice identifies Cambria, Comfort, Sleep Inn and Country Inn & Suites as new-hotel development brands, while Quality, Clarion and several other flags are more conversion-oriented. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1046311/000104631126000008/chh-20251231.htm))

## Practical “first-pass” shortlist

For a location-neutral international study, I would usually begin with:

1. **Hampton by Hilton**
2. **Hilton Garden Inn**
3. **Holiday Inn Express**
4. **Courtyard by Marriott**
5. **Fairfield by Marriott**
6. **Four Points by Sheraton**
7. **ibis or ibis Styles**
8. **Novotel**
9. **Hyatt Place**
10. **Wyndham Garden or La Quinta**
11. **Park Inn by Radisson**
12. One lifestyle alternative—usually **Moxy, Aloft, TRIBE, Caption** or **Radisson RED**

The final shortlist should then be narrowed by **market segment, room count, site efficiency, required F&B, construction cost per key, franchise versus management availability, loyalty contribution, territorial protection and expected fee load**. Brand rights also require geographic verification—for example, the Radisson brands are controlled by Choice Hotels in the Americas and by Radisson Hotel Group outside the Americas. ([choicehotels.com](https://www.choicehotels.com/about/brands?msockid=102f5d623ea6639f39a94bf93f5f62a0&utm_source=openai))
